author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: The Sony WH-1000XM6
recommendations.blurb: Sony’s over-ear headphones have been the best on the market for the last few years. The new ones aren’t exactly, you know, mind-blowing, and $450 is a lot, but I’ll take the improvements across the board — especially the better mics and noise cancelling.

recommendations.name: Doom: The Dark Ages
recommendations.blurb: The first Doom game in five years, and by all accounts it is much more than just a sequel. I’m no scholar in the series, but I’m into the idea that it both has a solid story and has ratcheted up the quality of the fighting. Get you a game that can do both, you know?

recommendations.name: Spotify’s AI DJ.
recommendations.blurb: Finally , this feature works the way it should. You can ask Spotify’s chatbot to play you songs based on an artist, or a mood, or whatever else you’re feeling, and it’ll generate endless music on the fly.

recommendations.name: Murderbot
recommendations.blurb: It’s dystopian, it’s funny, it’s occasionally pretty existential . It’s a story about life as a bot that would really just rather… not. Apple TV Plus continues to do sci-fi really well, and while I’ve seen a few folks who (as always) prefer the books , this is one to try this weekend.

recommendations.name: Love, Death & Robots season four
recommendations.blurb: This Netflix series is a very different take on robots. A bunch of big-name filmmakers made all kinds of exciting, bizarre sci-fi shorts that seem to cross every genre and style you can think of. David Fincher directed one! And I guarantee you’ll never guess what it is!

recommendations.name: The DJI Mavic 4 Pro
recommendations.blurb: With a 360-degree gimbal, long battery life, and a 100-megapixel camera, DJI continues to outdo itself on the drone front. Technically, if you’re in the US you’re not supposed to be able to buy this $2,700 model — but my colleague Sean Hollister found them on sale anyway .

recommendations.name: Internet Roadtrip
recommendations.blurb: There’s a new Neal.fun thing, so I’m going to tell you about the new Neal.fun thing. This one’s a tour through Street View in which everyone currently on the site gets to decide where we go next. Not quite as world-shattering as Stimulation Clicker , but still very good.

recommendations.name: Airbnb
recommendations.blurb: I’m not sure what to make of this huge pivot , honestly. Airbnb as a huge collection of travel experiences and services, rather than just homes, makes a certain kind of sense. But is this ultimately just, like, fancy Yelp? I don’t know. But I’m fascinated by how big a swing this is .

recommendations.name: Android 16
recommendations.blurb: I really like the new design language for Android, which is bold and colorful and gives both users and developers a lot more to play with. It all feels a little more… alive, when everything else about smartphones is starting to feel drab and stale.

recommendations.name: An iPhone 16 Pro I got earlier this year
recommendations.blurb: The phone: An iPhone 16 Pro I got earlier this year. I upgraded from an iPhone 12 Mini that I miss desperately — the iPhone 16 Pro is too heavy and too big for me.

recommendations.name: Days Since
recommendations.blurb: The countdown widget comes from an app called Days Since . I’m a newish dad to a very early riser, and I realized last year that even one glass of wine made me a step too slow to keep up with my active kid. I’ve set a goal to not drink for a year just to see if I can do it, and so far, so good.

recommendations.name: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
recommendations.blurb: I feel like my entire personality has become Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , a wonderful RPG that’s my favorite game of the year so far. It’s just so good. And the soundtrack is outstanding .

recommendations.name: Minimal Phone
recommendations.blurb: Received my new Minimal Phone a week ago and it is excellent. There are still some issues to be resolved, but overall there is a ton of potential for this concept of a smart dumb phone.

recommendations.name: Co-Intelligence: Living and Working with AI
recommendations.blurb: Currently reading: Co-Intelligence: Living and Working with AI by Ethan Mollick. It’s fantastic so far, and has already changed my mind a bit on the whole AI thing.

recommendations.name: Morsle
recommendations.blurb: Morsle , the daily word game that gives you the morse code of a 5 letter word to guess.

recommendations.name: Levels
recommendations.blurb: I was a user of Levels for a long time to track my glucose, but didn’t realize you can now buy a Dexcom Stelo for $80 on Amazon and it integrates into Oura ring to understand more about your holistic health. It’s a great alternative if you’re interested in tracking your glucose.

recommendations.name: Sony MDRZX110NC
recommendations.blurb: My fav cheap headphones that I use most days are the Sony MDRZX110NC , which are kind of noise cancelling, but nothing fancy. My ‘real’ headphones are the MDR-V6 and the long-discontinued MDR-V700DJ that I’ve mostly retired. Not really much of a wireless guy since I just like to plug stuff in.

recommendations.name: Subo
recommendations.blurb: Got the early bird access to Subo app! It’s an independent app to track your subscriptions, looks pretty too!

recommendations.name: Long Way Home
recommendations.blurb: The new season of Ewan McGregor and Charley Boorman’s motorbike travelogue show on Apple TV Plus has started, this time titled Long Way Home . Just a great show for lifting your spirits and for showing the joy of engaging with and enjoying other cultures.

recommendations.name: Siete Churro Strips
recommendations.blurb: I got the Siete Churro Strips from Wegman’s last week, and I’ve been crumbling them up and putting them on my vanilla ice cream at night. It’s so good to get that little bit of crunch with the vanilla ice cream.

recommendations.name: DisplayPort 1.2 cables
recommendations.blurb: Dialing in my work-from-home setup this week. How come no one talks about the fact that you can daisychain monitors with DisplayPort 1.2 cables ?! Also, I am shopping around for a footrest for underneath the desk, and I have no idea where to start.

recommendations.name: YouTube compilations
recommendations.blurb: I was in New York for a couple of days this week, working on a big new project I am very excited to share with all of you… later. One thing I got to do as part of the project was a deep dive into old Vines, and you know what? Vine was awesome, y’all.
